ing: or apple juice plus 1 tbsp lemon juice
cut into 1 inch cubes, slightly stale
st: Rub the inside of a heavy pot with the cut sides of the garlic clove, then discard it.
Toss the shredded cheeses with the cornstarch until evenly coated.
Pour in [[1 cup]] wine and [[1 tsp]] lemon juice. Warm over medium heat until it is steaming but not boiling.
Add the cheese a handful at a time, stirring in a figure-eight pattern and waiting for each addition to melt.
Keep the heat low and stir for about 8 minutes until smooth and thick. Do not let it boil.
Stir in the kirsch if using, plus the pepper and nutmeg.
Move the pot to a burner or fondue stand on low heat to keep it warm.
Spear bread cubes with forks and dip, stirring the pot as you go so the cheese stays smooth.
Put the potatoes in a pot with [[8 cups]] cold water and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil.
Simmer for 20 minutes until a knife slides in easily.
Drain and keep warm in a covered dish or wrapped in a towel.
Set out the pickles and pearl onions in small bowls.
Heat the oven broiler or a raclette grill. Place small pans with a slice of cheese each.
Melt the cheese for 3 to 4 minutes, until bubbling with golden edges.
Scrape the melted cheese over the warm potatoes on each plate.
Season with the pepper and paprika and serve with the pickles. Repeat with more cheese.
Boil the whole unpeeled potatoes in lightly salted water for 12 minutes, until just barely tender. Drain and cool completely, ideally overnight.
Peel the potatoes and grate them on the large holes of a box grater.
Cook the chopped bacon in a skillet over medium heat for 6 minutes until crisp. Add the onion and cook 3 minutes. Remove both to a plate.
Toss the grated potato with [[1 tsp]] salt, [[0.5 tsp]] pepper, and the bacon and onion.
Melt [[1.5 tbsp]] butter in a 10 inch nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Press the potato into the pan in an even layer. Do not pack it too hard.
Cook for 12 minutes until the bottom is deep golden. Slide onto a plate.
Add [[1.5 tbsp]] butter to the pan, flip the rösti back in, and cook 10 minutes more.
Slide onto a board, cut into wedges and serve hot.

ing: sliced into thin strips; or pork loin
st: Pat the veal dry and toss with the flour, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Melt [[1 tbsp]] butter in a large skillet over high heat. Sear half the veal for 1 to 2 minutes until just browned and move to a plate.
Repeat with another [[1 tbsp]] butter and the rest of the veal. Cooking it quickly keeps it tender.
Add the last [[1 tbsp]] butter and cook the mushrooms for 5 minutes until golden.
Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes until soft.
Pour in [[0.5 cup]] wine and scrape the pan. Boil for 2 minutes to reduce by half.
Add [[1 cup]] cream and simmer for 4 minutes until slightly thick.
Return the veal and juices to the pan, warm 1 minute, and season with [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Sprinkle with the parsley and serve with rösti.
Bring [[8 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt to a boil in a large pot.
Add the potatoes and boil for 6 minutes.
Add the macaroni to the same pot and cook for 8 more minutes, until both are tender. Drain well.
Meanwhile, melt [[3 tbsp]] butter in a skillet over medium-low heat. Cook the onions for 20 minutes, stirring, until deep golden and sweet.
Return the drained pasta and potatoes to the pot over low heat.
Stir in [[1 cup]] cream, [[0.5 tsp]] salt, [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and the cheese until melted and creamy, about 3 minutes.
Spoon into bowls and top with the browned onions.
Serve hot with applesauce on the side.
Whisk [[2 cups]] flour, the eggs, [[0.5 cup]] of the milk, [[0.5 tsp]] salt, the pepper and nutmeg until a thick batter forms. Add up to [[0.25 cup]] more milk to loosen.
Stir in the chopped dried beef and parsley.
Blanch the chard leaves in boiling water for 30 seconds, then cool in cold water and pat dry.
Place a spoonful of batter on each leaf, fold in the sides and roll up like a small packet.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Arrange the packets seam-side down in a buttered baking dish.
Pour in [[1 cup]] chicken broth and [[0.5 cup]] cream around them. Sprinkle with [[0.5 cup]] of the cheese.
Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes.
Remove the foil, add the remaining cheese and bake 10 more minutes until bubbling and golden.
Rest 5 minutes and serve hot.
Stir the oats, milk and yogurt together in a bowl.
Mix in the lemon juice and honey.
Cover and chill for at least 8 hours, or overnight, so the oats soften.
Just before serving, grate the apple, skin on, and squeeze with extra lemon juice to keep it from browning.
Fold the grated apple into the oats.
Loosen with a splash more milk if too thick.
Spoon into bowls and top with the nuts and berries.
Stir the yeast and sugar into [[1 cup]] warm milk. Wait 8 minutes until foamy.
Mix in one egg and the softened butter, then add the flour and salt.
Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and soft. Add flour by spoonfuls only if too sticky.
Cover and let rise for 1.5 hours, until doubled.
Divide the dough into 2 pieces, with one slightly larger. Cut each into 3 ropes, roll each 14 inches long.
Braid the 3 ropes of the larger piece. Braid the smaller one and lay it on top, tucking the ends under.
Place on a lined baking sheet, cover, and let rise 45 minutes.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Beat the second egg with [[1 tbsp]] milk and brush the loaf.
Bake for 35 minutes until golden brown and hollow-sounding when tapped.
Cool on a rack before slicing.
Warm the honey and [[0.5 cup]] sugar in a saucepan over low heat until the sugar dissolves. Let it cool until just warm.
Mix the flour, almonds, candied peel, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg and baking soda in a big bowl.
Stir in the honey mixture and the kirsch (or [[2 tbsp]] water) to form a stiff dough.
Wrap the dough and rest overnight, or at least 1 hour, in the fridge.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Roll the dough on a floured sheet of parchment to 0.5 inch thick.
Bake the dough slab on the sheet for 20 minutes until firm and lightly browned.
Whisk [[1 cup]] powdered sugar with [[3 tbsp]] water until smooth.
Brush the glaze over the hot slab, then cool 10 minutes.
Cut into rectangles about 1 by 2 inches. Store airtight for a few days to soften.
Mix the flour, powdered sugar and salt. Rub in the cold butter until crumbly, then mix in the egg to form a dough.
Divide into one-third and two-thirds, wrap and chill for 1 hour.
Melt [[1 cup]] sugar in a heavy saucepan over medium heat, without stirring until amber, about 8 minutes.
Add [[2 tbsp]] honey, then slowly pour in [[0.5 cup]] cream, standing back as it will bubble. Stir until smooth.
Stir in the walnuts and cool the filling for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Roll the larger dough piece and fit into a 9 inch tart pan.
Spoon in the walnut filling. Roll out the smaller piece for a lid, press edges to seal and trim.
Prick the lid with a fork and brush with the beaten yolk.
Bake for 35 minutes until golden. Cool completely in the pan before slicing.
Place the chopped chocolate in a heatproof bowl.
Heat the cream in a small pot over medium heat until it just starts to steam at the edges, about 4 minutes. Do not let it boil.
Pour the hot cream over the chocolate, wait 2 minutes, then stir slowly from the center until perfectly smooth.
Stir in the butter, kirsch and salt. Cover and chill for 2 hours until firm enough to scoop.
Scoop with a small spoon and roll into rough balls with cool hands, working quickly.
Roll each truffle in the cocoa powder. Keep chilled and serve at room temperature.
nt: Best swap: use coconut cream for the cream and dairy-free dark chocolate, or orange liqueur instead of kirsch.
